headline: Andrea Kimi Antonelli won his home race at Monza from 19th on the grid after taking advantage of a late Safety Car.
whatHappened: Surprise pole-sitter Pierre Gasly dropped back early as George Russell and Max Verstappen set the pace at the front. A mid-race engine failure for Charles Leclerc brought out a Safety Car, neutralizing the field just as long-running drivers needed to pit. Antonelli, who started 19th following an engine penalty, pitted under the neutralization for fresh soft tyres while those ahead were on older hards. He swept past Verstappen and Russell in the final ten laps to secure a Mercedes one-two finish.
keyBattle: The race hinged on Mercedes' decision to extend Antonelli's initial hard-tyre stint past lap 30 instead of locking him into a traffic-heavy two-stop strategy. When Leclerc stopped on track, Antonelli gained a low-cost pit stop that erased a 20-second gap to track leader Russell.
championshipImpact: Antonelli extended his drivers' championship lead over teammate Russell to 66 points. Leclerc's engine failure dropped him to fifth in the standings, 112 points off the lead and virtually out of contention.
watchThis: Watch how Antonelli managed tyre temperatures while trailing traffic through the Parabolica in his opening stint. Keeping the rear tyres under control early allowed him to extend the stint until the Safety Car fell into his window.
